info.title: Quak API
info.description:
The Quak API plays announcements on Sonos speakers: text-to-speech, sounds, own clips, files, URLs and push-to-talk, with voice effects and ambiences, quiet hours and a live history.

## Before you start

1. An account: sign up at https://quak.party (or `POST /v1/user/signup`).
2. Sonos connected to the workspace: in the app or on the website, the Sonos login runs in a browser (`GET /v1/sonos/connect` gives the link).
3. An API key: in the app under API keys (`POST /v1/keys`), or the login key from `POST /v1/user/login/key`.

Then `POST /v1/play/text` with `{ "text": "Hello" }` plays on the workspace's default speakers; `GET /v1/speakers` lists the slugs for `to`.

## Requests

- Unknown fields in a request are ignored, not refused, so a newer client works with an older server.
- `PATCH` changes only the fields you send: a missing field stays, `null` sets it back to its default where the field allows `null`.

Send bodies as JSON with the header `Content-Type: application/json` (curl's `--json` sets it, in other tools such as Shortcuts, Postman or Zapier set it yourself). Uploads (`POST /v1/play/file`, `POST /v1/play/talk`, `POST /v1/clips`) go as `multipart/form-data` (curl `-F`). Simple GET parameters also work in the query string.

```sh
curl -X POST https://api.quak.party/v1/play/sound \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $QUAK_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"sound":"quakquak"}'
```

## Authentication

To get an API key:

1. Call `POST /v1/user/signup` (new account) or `POST /v1/user/login` with your email address.
2. Confirm the request via the email link.
3. Exchange the `verifyToken` using `POST /v1/user/login/key` to receive your API key.

Scripts, integrations and AI agents can also use a key made in the Quak app (or with `POST /v1/keys`); the login is for apps that sign a person in.

Use the API key on protected endpoints with either:

- Header: `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` (raw token also works). Recommended.
- Query parameter: `?apikey=<API_KEY>`, handy for demos and quick tests. A key in a URL can end up in logs, the browser history and referrers of the tools on the way, so use the header in integrations.

API keys look like `qk_key_…` (43 characters). The full key is shown once, when it is made (`POST /v1/keys`, `POST /v1/user/login/key`); Quak only keeps a hash of it. Lists show its start (`qk_key_7Fh2…`).

## Workspaces, roles and scopes

A workspace holds the credits and subscription, the Sonos accounts and speakers, groups, clips, keys and the playback defaults (`GET /v1/workspace`). Every user gets a personal workspace at sign-up and can be a member of more (`GET /v1/workspaces`, invitations with `POST /v1/workspace/invites`); plays keep who triggered them.

Which workspace a request works in: a **login key** (from logging in with an app, the website or the CLI) belongs to you, not to a workspace. Name the workspace per request with the header `X-Quak-Workspace: <slug or id>`; without it the request works in the workspace you named last, else your personal one. Switching needs no new login. A key made with `POST /v1/keys` belongs to one workspace; a header naming another one is `403 ERROR_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH`. The workspace of a request is in the `X-Quak-Workspace-UUID` header of the answer.

Both have to allow a request: the key's **scope** and your **role** in the workspace. Scopes include the ones below: `play` (read speakers, voices, sounds, credits, history and play, costs credits) < `create` (and add clips: upload one or keep a play as one) < `manage` (and settings, Sonos accounts, keys, groups, renaming and deleting clips, members). Keys made with `POST /v1/keys` get `play` unless asked otherwise, login keys `manage`. Roles: `MEMBER` reads and plays (and adds clips); `ADMIN` also runs the workspace, several admins are equal. Changing the email and creating workspaces need a login key. Every endpoint names its scope; with too little the answer is `403 ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, with a role too low `403 ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_ROLE`, both with the need in `details.required`.

## Identifiers

- `id`: stable UUID identifier exposed in public API payloads.
- `slug`: human-friendly identifier on slug-enabled resources (for example Sonos accounts).

For slug-enabled resources, `/{id}` path params can accept either `id` or `slug`.

## Playback

Play text (`POST /v1/play/text`), built-in sounds, own clips, URLs, uploaded files and what someone said into a mic (`POST /v1/play/talk` after release, `GET /v1/play/talk/live` as a WebSocket while talking) on your Sonos speakers. Missing parameters come from the workspace defaults (`PATCH /v1/workspace/defaults`), including quiet hours (default `22-7`, in the workspace time zone): a play during quiet hours is not played, costs nothing and returns `200` with status `SKIPPED`. `preview: true` only produces the audio and returns its `audioUrl`. Every play is kept in the history (`GET /v1/plays`) and can be stopped while it runs.

Credits: 1 when Sonos fetches from the CDN or the source (sound, clip, URL without processing), 2 when the audio goes through the API server (TTS, processed URL, file, talk), plus the voice rate per started 100 characters for TTS and 1 per started 10 s of speech for talk. A TTS cache hit (same text and voice within the workspace's audio cache time, `audioCacheMinutes` in `PATCH /v1/workspace`) costs 2, the preview skips the base fee. The balance after the play is in the `X-Quak-Credits` header.

## Audio formats

Everything Quak plays is mono, a Sonos room plays on one speaker (a stereo pair only on the left one), so mono uploads lose nothing.

- **Uploads** (`POST /v1/play/file`, `POST /v1/play/talk`, `POST /v1/clips`): any common audio format, for example MP3, M4A/AAC, Opus (WebM or Ogg), WAV or FLAC, max. 10 MB and 180 s. Prefer a compressed format (MP3, M4A, Opus): a WAV of 180 s is about 15 MB mono and does not fit, an MP3 at 128 kbit/s is about 3 MB. For talk the browser's `MediaRecorder` output (WebM/Opus) or iOS M4A can be sent as is.
- **URLs with processing** (`POST /v1/play/url`, default): like uploads, the server downloads and converts them.
- **URLs without processing** (`process: false`): Sonos fetches the file itself, so it must be **MP3** (or WAV) on a public HTTPS URL. Use MP3: Sonos does not play WAV files shorter than about one second.
- **What Sonos gets** from Quak is MP3 (128 kbit/s, 44.1 kHz, mono) for generated audio, sounds and clips.

## Responses

The API can return these status codes across endpoints:

- `200 OK`: request succeeded.
- `201 Created`: a resource was created (for example an API key).
- `202 Accepted`: request is valid but completion is still pending (for example login confirmation wait mode).
- `204 No Content`: request succeeded and no response body is returned (typically delete endpoints).
- `302 Found`: redirect response (for example Sonos connect with `redirect=1`).
- `400 Bad Request`: a parameter is missing or not valid (`field` names it), or the body is not readable.
- `401 Unauthorized`: API key missing, invalid or deleted (log in again), or an expired/invalid login verify token.
- `402 Payment Required`: not enough credits for the play.
- `403 Forbidden`: the API key is valid but may not do this.
- `404 Not Found`: requested resource does not exist in your scope.
- `409 Conflict`: uniqueness conflict (for example duplicate API key name) or a play that is not running any more.
- `424 Failed Dependency`: no speaker accepted the play (for example offline or gone), or Sonos did not let it stop.
- `429 Too Many Requests`: a rate limit was hit, wait `Retry-After` seconds.
- `503 Service Unavailable`: a service behind Quak failed, for example Sonos or the speech synthesis. Quak never answers with 502 or 504.

Every error has the same body, the schema `Error`: `{ "error": { "code": "ERROR_…", "message": "…", "field": "…", "requestId": "…" } }`. Check `code`, it is stable; `message` is for people.

## Rate limits

Generous limits guard against floods and loops, not against normal use. Each answer of a limited route says where you stand, with the headers of the IETF draft: `RateLimit-Policy: "tts";q=30;w=60` (30 requests per 60 seconds in the group `tts`) and `RateLimit: "tts";r=29;t=42` (29 left, the window ends in 42 seconds). Over the limit: `429 ERROR_RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`.

- Login and sign-up: per IP and per address.
- Speech (`POST /v1/play/text`) and the other plays: per workspace.
- Everything else with a key: per key.

## Retries

A play that timed out may still have played. To retry it safely, send the header `Idempotency-Key` with your own ID (a UUID) on the plays, `POST /v1/plays/{id}/replay`, `POST /v1/plays/{id}/save` and `POST /v1/clips`. The same key within 24 hours returns the first answer again, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and nothing plays or costs twice. Only a success is kept; after an error the next try runs normally.

- `409 ERROR_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`: the first request is still running, wait `Retry-After` seconds.
- `409 ERROR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`: the key belongs to another request. Use a new key for every play.

## Versions

The version is part of the path. `/v1` is stable to build on. New routes, fields, error codes and enum values (a play `status`, a `platform`, a `type`, a voice `provider` …) can come at any time, so a client must not break on them:

- ignore fields you don't know,
- treat an unknown enum value like an unknown one in the UI (show it as is, or as other), never as an error,
- treat an unknown `code` like its HTTP status.

tags.description:
Services connected to the workspace that play through Quak, with its credits and defaults:

- **Slack** (`slack`): “Add to Slack”, then everyone in the Slack workspace plays with `/quak <text>`.
- **IFTTT** (`ifttt`): the Quak service on IFTTT, applets play text, sounds and clips.

Sonos is not one of them, it has its own routes (Sonos).

Scope: `manage`. Admins of the workspace only. Switches the running subscription.

- **Upgrade** (a bigger plan, monthly → yearly): at once, the difference is charged now. In the trial at once and free; Business ends the trial.
- **Downgrade**: at the end of the period. The usage must fit the smaller plan, else `409 ERROR_OVER_PLAN_LIMITS` with `details.blockedBy` (as in the preview) until locations, members, invitations and triggers are within its limits.

get.description:
**WebSocket.** Connect to `wss://<host>/v1/play/talk/live` (a GET with `Upgrade: websocket`), not a plain HTTP request. The protocol is below.

Beta, may change without notice. Plays what someone says while they say it.

### 1. Start

Every message, both ways, is `{ "type": …, "data": {…} }`; an error is `{ "type": "error", "error": { code, message, field, requestId } }` like a REST error. The first message, as text, within 2 s:

```json
{ "type": "start", "data": { "apiKey": "qk_key_…", "to": ["kitchen"], "format": { "encoding": "opus", "sampleRate": 48000 } } }
```

- `format.encoding`: `opus`, `pcm_s16le` or `pcm_f32le`; `format.sampleRate`: `16000`, `24000`, `44100` or `48000`.
- Optional, as with the other plays: `volume`, `volumes`, `effect`, `effectIntensity`, `ambience`, `ambienceIntensity`, `intro`, `outro`, `gap`, `priority`, `quietHours`.
- Instead of `apiKey`: the `Authorization` header on the handshake (native clients). From a browser that should not see the key: `"token": "qk_ptk_…"`, a play token from `POST /v1/play-tokens` (5 minutes, it names the workspace; an invalid one closes with `4401` and `ERROR_INVALID_TOKEN`).
- A login key names its workspace with `"workspace": "<slug or id>"` in `data`, `?workspace=` or `X-Quak-Workspace`.

### 2. Talk

The answer is `{"type":"ready","data":{"play":{…},"creditsUsed":2,"balance":…,"maxSeconds":180}}` (`creditsUsed`: charged so far, `balance`: the workspace's credits). During quiet hours it is `{"type":"skipped","data":{…}}` instead and the socket closes, at no cost.

Send the audio as binary frames, in the format of the start: Opus one raw 20 ms packet per frame, PCM mono little endian. Audio sent before `ready` is kept (up to 5 s).

Change things while talking:

```json
{ "type": "update", "data": { "effect": "none", "muted": true } }
```

→ `{"type":"updated","data":{…}}` with the current values. Fields: `effect`, `effectIntensity`, `ambience`, `ambienceIntensity`, `muted`. The server sends `{"type":"ping"}` every 25 s.

### 3. End

```json
{ "type": "end" }
```

→ `{"type":"done","data":{"play":{…},"creditsUsed":…,"balance":…,"endedBy":"CLIENT"}}`, then the socket closes. `creditsUsed` is what the whole talk cost, `balance` the workspace's credits after the charge; `endedBy` is `CLIENT`, `DISCONNECTED`, `LIMIT` or `CREDITS`. Closing the socket also ends the talk.

### Limits, errors, credits

- At most 3 minutes. 30 s before, a warning comes: `{"type":"warning","data":{"code":"LIMIT_SOON","message":"Talk live ends in 30 s (max. 3 minutes).","secondsLeft":30}}`.
- Faster, slower and reverse do not work live.
- Errors: `{"type":"error","error":{"code":…,"message":…,"field":…,"requestId":…}}`, then the socket closes with 4000 + the HTTP status (e.g. `4402` without credits).
- Credits: 2 at the start, and the workspace needs enough for a minute of speech. After the end 1 per started 10 s of speech. If the credits no longer cover the next minute, a warning with `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` comes and the talk ends.

get.description:
**WebSocket.** Connect to `wss://<host>/v1/plays/watch` (a GET with `Upgrade: websocket`), not a plain HTTP request. The protocol is below.

Live status of your plays: every running play once, then every change.

### 1. Log in

Every message is `{ "type": …, "data": {…} }`, an error `{ "type": "error", "error": { code, message } }`. The first message, as text, within 5 s:

```json
{ "type": "auth", "data": { "apiKey": "qk_key_…" } }
```

- Instead of `apiKey`: the `Authorization` header on the handshake (native clients). From a browser that should not see the key: `"token": "qk_ptk_…"`, a play token from `POST /v1/play-tokens` (5 minutes, it names the workspace; an invalid one closes with `4401` and `ERROR_INVALID_TOKEN`).
- A login key watches the workspace named by `"workspace"` in its `data`, `?workspace=` or `X-Quak-Workspace` (slug or id), else the last used one.
- No or a wrong key closes with `4001`.

### 2. Receive

```json
{ "type": "ready" }
{ "type": "play", "data": { "id": "…", "status": "ACTIVE", … } }
{ "type": "ping" }
```

- `play`: every running play once, then every change, the same object as `GET /v1/plays/:id`. Plays with `test: true` are trigger tests from the app and not part of the history.
- `trigger_call`: with a `manage` key and the admin role also every call of a trigger URL, the same object as `GET /v1/triggers/:id/calls`.
- `ping` every 25 s, so proxies keep the connection.

Reconnect after a drop: you get the current state again.

post.description:
Scope: `play`. Plays the audio of a play once more, exactly as it played (intro, outro and effect included): what someone said into the mic, a preview on the speakers, or again in another room.

- Speakers, volume, volumes, priority and quiet hours are the ones of the play unless the body names others. The content cannot change: for another effect play it again (a text reuses its speech).
- A new play in the history with `params.replayOf`.
- Works for sounds and clips, and for text, talk, file and processed URL plays while their audio is there (the audio cache time), else `409 ERROR_AUDIO_GONE`. Not for talk live and URL plays without processing (`400 ERROR_NOT_REPLAYABLE`).
- Credits: only the base fee, 1 for sounds and clips, 2 for the rest.

Scope: `manage`. Admins of the workspace only. Beta, may change without notice. A secret URL that plays an announcement without an API key, for anything that can call a URL: a doorbell, a button, a shortcut, a webhook.

- Call it with `GET` or `POST`. The answer and every later read have `url`.
- It plays its own text, sound or clip, or one entry of a rule's pool (`rules`: if/then by event, values of the call, day and hour).
- Each play costs credits like any play. Cooldown, daily limit and allowed websites limit what a leaked URL can do.
- How many a workspace may have depends on the plan (Home 3, Family 10, Team 30, Business 100, none without a plan): above it `403 ERROR_PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED` with `limit`, `used`, `allowed` and `requiredPlan` in `details`.

post.description:
Scope: `play`. A short-lived token for a browser that should not see the API key: a key is permanent and secret, a token temporary.

1. Your server gets the token with its key.
2. It hands the token to the browser.
3. The browser plays straight at the API with `Authorization: Bearer qk_ptk_…`, and on the WebSockets (talk live, live status) with `"token": "qk_ptk_…"` in the first message.

- Opens only `POST /v1/play/text`, `/v1/play/sound`, `/v1/play/clip`, `/v1/play/url`, `/v1/play/file`, `/v1/play/talk`, `/v1/play/stop`, `/v1/plays/{id}/stop` and `/v1/plays/{id}/replay`. `GET /v1/play/talk/live` and `GET /v1/plays/watch` take it too. Any other route: `403 ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`.
- Works any number of times for 5 minutes, in the workspace of this request (`X-Quak-Workspace`) and with the rights of this key. Plays count as plays of this key and, unless they name a client themselves, as plays of the client of this request (`User-Agent: quak-<name>/<version>` or `X-Quak-Client`): a browser behind the Home Assistant integration plays as `HOME_ASSISTANT`.
- Expired, unknown, or the key was signed out: `401 ERROR_INVALID_TOKEN` (on a WebSocket: closes with `4401`). Get a new token and try once more.
- Send it in the header or the first message, not in a URL: it works more than once, so it stays out of addresses and logs.
